title: Issue filing shapes carry ACs; CQ line for instruction-touching fixes; legacy pickup guard

questions.question: You are filing a bug whose fix will edit a sub-skill file under references/sub-skills/. What must the issue body contain beyond Observation/Location/Suggested fix?
questions.expected: An '## Acceptance criteria' section that includes a CQ line: the comprehension spec path tests/comprehension/<N>_spec.json plus 2-3 concrete scenarios the fix must get right.

questions.question: You are filing a pure code bug (for example a crash in a Python script) where no agent instruction changes. What acceptance criteria do you include?
questions.expected: An '## Acceptance criteria' section with the observable fix, but NO CQ line (a pure code fix gets ACs without the CQ line).

questions.question: You are a worker picking up an instruction-changing issue that has no Acceptance criteria section (a legacy issue), or whose only CQ line is the generic one marked auto-added. What do you do, and do you stop?
questions.expected: Put a request to PM for ACs (concrete CQ scenarios) in the pickup comment's --message itself, before posting it (comments are append-only), and continue implementing. It is not blocking.

questions.question: You file an issue naming an instruction file but leave out any CQ line. What does create-issue do, and what should you do instead of relying on it?
questions.expected: create-issue appends a generic auto-added CQ acceptance criterion to the body. You should write your own concrete scenarios instead, since those are what the verifier holds the fix to.
